title: Added functionality to support style keyword
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

This change allows users to use syntax such as:

`style CLASSNAME fill:#000,stroke:2px`

in order to apply css styles to individual class boxes

Resolves #2408

### Example

Rendering the following Mermaid diagram will look like:

> ````markdown
> ```mermaid
>  classDiagram 
>    class Animal 
>    class Mineral 
>    style Animal fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px 
>    style Mineral fill:#bbf,stroke:#f66,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff,stroke-dasharray: 5 5 
> ```
> ````
> 
> ![image](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/assets/19716675/c3390966-7f4c-448c-b749-6d573ef3284e)
>

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: Is `BRKT` a common abbreviation of `#`? I was only aware of Hash and Pound.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
This might be a dumb question, since I'm not super experienced with JISON, but aren't both of these lines identical?

`\#` should be equivalent to `"#"`

---

Also, fun fact of the day (since I just learnt this too), apparently the `#` sign comes from `℔` which comes from lb, which is what Americans use as a unit of mass!

And you can also call it octothorpe if you want to be really fancy :)

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
We have a custom syntax for notes that you can use:

````suggestion
```note
When a generic is used within a class definition, the generic type is NOT considered part of the class name. i.e.: for any syntax which required you to reference the class name, you need to drop the type part of the definition. This also means that mermaid does not currently support having two classes with the same name, but different generic types.
```
````

It will make it look something like the following:

![image](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/assets/19716675/ef0d3c52-e56a-4e9f-94a1-d6c806d6edbb)


See https://mermaid.js.org/community/documentation.html#how-to-contribute-to-documentation for more info.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests using a custom note syntax for documentation formatting and provides a code suggestion.
